checks: Real provider-issued tokens execute MCP and persist the consenting user and OAuth client in audit
Deny consent returns no code; signed-query tampering and missing-origin consent are rejected
Code exchange rejects wrong verifier, redirect, resource, client and already-consumed code
Members and foreign teams cannot manage clients; native privilege escalation, unsafe callbacks, machine grants and session cookies on machine endpoints fail
OAuth discovery and cached aliases obey the same current user tool permissions as API keys and chat
Native refresh rotation changes both tokens; reuse of the old refresh token invalidates the family
Native access revocation rejects the next MCP request; refresh revocation also removes family access
Disabling a client immediately rejects existing bearer access and re-enabling restores a still-valid grant
Inactive membership rejects an otherwise valid OAuth grant on its next request
Signing out the authorizing session makes its previously working OAuth access inactive
A token issued with the production 300-second TTL expires naturally and fails the real gateway; no clock or database expiry manipulation
Existing personal API-key clients remain interoperable after OAuth denial and revocation tests
